issues.text: Two very large trials found vitamin D tablets did not prevent broken bones. The people in them were mostly healthy, and most were not short of vitamin D.
issues.problem: Attributes 'mostly not short of vitamin D' to both trials; baseline vitamin D status for D-Health was not verified (claim C04-20-c qualification forbids it). Only VITAL is supported.
issues.source_says: C04-20-c: baseline vitamin D status not in abstract, so do not describe D-Health participants as 'having enough' without qualification.
issues.replacement: Two very large trials found vitamin D tablets did not prevent broken bones. The people in them were mostly healthy, and in VITAL most were not short of vitamin D.

issues.text: Two very large trials found vitamin D tablets did not prevent broken bones. The people in them were mostly healthy, and most were not short of vitamin D. Both facts belong in the headline.
issues.replacement: Two very large trials found vitamin D tablets did not prevent broken bones. The people in them were mostly healthy, and in VITAL most were not short of vitamin D. Both facts belong in the headline.

issues.text: Most were healthy and not short of vitamin D.
issues.problem: Same overstatement applied to all 45,000 across both trials.
issues.source_says: C04-20-b/c: 'not deficient' verified for VITAL only.
issues.replacement: Most were healthy, and in VITAL most were not short of vitamin D.

issues.text: Most people in them were healthy and not short of vitamin D.
issues.replacement: Most people in them were healthy, and in VITAL most were not short of vitamin D.

issues.text: Vitamin D with calcium slightly cut hip fractures in pooled trials, more so in care homes.
issues.problem: 'More so' implies a larger effect in care homes; the per-1000 figures apply one pooled relative risk to a higher assumed baseline risk.
issues.source_says: Avenell 2014: RR 0.84 overall; 1 vs 9 fewer per 1000 are estimates from assumed baseline risks of 8 and 54 per 1000.
issues.replacement: Vitamin D with calcium slightly cut hip fractures in pooled trials; because hip fractures are more common in care homes, more are estimated to be prevented there.

issues.text: For approved drugs, density gains do track fracture reduction across whole trials. In one person, much less so: with alendronate, the spine density gain accounted for about 16% of the fall in spinal fractures.
issues.problem: The 16% is a trial-level proportion of the alendronate benefit explained by spine density, not a measure of how well density predicts benefit in one person. Presents a trial-level statistic as individual-level evidence.
issues.source_says: Cummings 2002: 'In the Fracture Intervention Trial, improvement in spine bone mineral density explained 16% ... of the reduction in the risk of vertebral fracture with alendronate.' The individual-level point comes from Bell 2009 (scan variation larger than between-person differences).
issues.replacement: For approved drugs, density gains do track fracture reduction across whole trials. But density explains only part of the benefit: with alendronate, the spine density gain accounted for about 16% of the fall in spinal fractures. And a repeat scan in one person varies more than the real differences between people.

issues.text: In one person it explains little: with alendronate, about 16% of the fall in spinal fractures.
issues.problem: Same conflation of a trial-level proportion with an individual prediction.
issues.source_says: Cummings 2002 trial-level 16%; Bell 2009 for individual scans.
issues.replacement: But density explains only part of the benefit: with alendronate, about 16% of the fall in spinal fractures. One person's repeat scan varies more than the real differences between people.

issues.text: In one person it is a weaker guide. With alendronate, the spine density gain accounted for about 16% of the fall in spinal fractures.
issues.problem: Presents the 16% as evidence about individuals.
issues.replacement: It also explains only part of the benefit: with alendronate, the spine density gain accounted for about 16% of the fall in spinal fractures. In one person it is a weaker guide still.

issues.text: In 1990, fluoride raised spine density by 35% but did not cut spinal fractures; other fractures rose (72 v 24).
issues.problem: 'Rose' implies a within-arm increase; 72 v 24 is a between-group count of fractures, not women. Missing 'more than placebo'.
issues.source_says: Riggs 1990: 'number of nonvertebral fractures was higher in the treatment group (72 vs. 24)'.
issues.replacement: In a 1990 trial, fluoride raised spine density 35% more than placebo but did not cut spinal fractures; there were more other fractures (72 v 24 fractures).

issues.text: In US records, 19 in 100 men treated had broken a bone after 5 years, against 13 in 100 untreated, a link rather than proof.
issues.problem: Figures apply only to men with prostate cancer who survived at least 5 years after diagnosis (a subgroup), not a 5-year cumulative risk for all treated men.
issues.source_says: Shahinian 2005: 'Of men surviving at least five years after diagnosis, 19.4 percent of those who received androgen-deprivation therapy had a fracture, as compared with 12.6 percent'.
issues.replacement: In US records of men with prostate cancer who lived at least 5 years, 19 in 100 who had hormone treatment had broken a bone, against 13 in 100 who did not, a link rather than proof.

issues.text: Men, 5 years on: 19 in 100 treated v 13 in 100 untreated broke a bone (link, not proof)
issues.problem: Same subgroup presented as a 5-year risk.
issues.replacement: Men with prostate cancer who lived 5+ years: 19 in 100 with hormone treatment v 13 in 100 without had broken a bone (link, not proof)

issues.text: Among men surviving 5 years, 19 in 100 treated v 13 in 100 untreated broke a bone (observational).
issues.problem: Should say 'at least 5 years' and 'with prostate cancer'.
issues.replacement: Among men with prostate cancer who lived at least 5 years, 19 in 100 who had hormone treatment v 13 in 100 who did not had broken a bone (observational).

issues.text: In trials, a year of bisphosphonate treatment spared about 1 in 100 women a non-spinal fracture. For someone likely to live only months, the weekly tablet routine may not help in time. Stopping can be right.
issues.problem: Omits the necessary qualification that trial women were 63 to 74 and not near the end of life; short version generalises.
issues.source_says: Deardorff 2022: 10 RCTs, mean ages 63 to 74; C04-04-a qualification.
issues.replacement: In trials of women aged 63 to 74 on average, a year of bisphosphonate treatment spared about 1 in 100 a non-spinal fracture. For someone likely to live only months, the weekly tablet routine may not help in time. Stopping can be right.

issues.text: The balance stays favourable: an estimated 149 hip fractures prevented for 2 atypical fractures per 10,000 White women over 3 years.
issues.problem: Missing that these are modelled estimates for women with osteoporosis, and that the balance was less favourable in Asian women.
issues.source_says: Black 2020: after 3 years, 149 hip fractures prevented and 2 atypical in Whites, 91 and 8 in Asians (modelled).
issues.replacement: The balance stays favourable: modelled estimates give 149 hip fractures prevented for 2 atypical fractures per 10,000 White women with osteoporosis over 3 years (less favourable, but still positive, in Asian women).

issues.text: An estimated 149 hip fractures are prevented for 2 atypical fractures per 10,000 White women over 3 years.
issues.replacement: Modelled estimates: 149 hip fractures prevented for 2 atypical fractures per 10,000 White women with osteoporosis over 3 years.

issues.text: If it lapses, bone loss returns within months and spinal fractures rise.
issues.problem: Fracture rise stated without noting it comes from a later analysis in women; slight compression.
issues.source_says: Cummings 2018 post hoc analysis, postmenopausal women.
issues.replacement: If it lapses, bone loss returns within months, and in a trial follow-up spinal fractures rose.

issues.text: That was the right point to make, and it needs a qualification.
issues.problem: Refers to an unspecified earlier statement; reads as if responding to someone. Not a factual claim but confusing.
issues.replacement: That is right, and it needs a qualification.
